correctness.rationale: The bilinear product formula makes the rank-one left-multiplication locus exactly U union V; hence automorphisms must preserve or exchange the bipartition. Full block equations give A^t A=beta I, B^t B=alpha I, Au0=alpha u0, Bv0=beta v0. Invertibility of r and s forces beta=alpha^2, alpha=beta^2 and alpha^3=1, then orthogonal decomposition gives precisely the stated group. At the identity over general rings, mixed-block Leibniz equations kill offdiagonal entries on the open where A and B invertible, giving local mu3 times two smooth orthogonal group schemes. The derivative of these equations gives 3a=0 and exactly one extra characteristic-three tangent direction. Gram determinants of restricted forms are r and s, giving the published finite orthogonal-group order formulas. Actual local verify.py independently enumerated K22 over three finite fields and row-reduced Leibniz matrices for seven other parameter cases, and printed VERIFY_OK. These computations are corroboration, not infinite proof.

originality.rationale: Giacomelli 2026 Definition 8.4 and Open Problem 6 motivate the question but give no full K_nn automorphism calculation. The full 2025 graph-automorphism article yields only the diagonal mu_3 subgroup and a graph-symmetry action; no full orthogonal group factors or characteristic-three tangent calculation. The 2019 Elduque–Labra group-scheme theorem is explicitly confined to perfect evolution algebras, whereas these bipartite evolution algebras have square rank two. Full-text and semantic-record checks found no statement implying the new whole-family theorem. Residual older-literature risk is recorded; a failed search is not asserted to prove novelty.

value.rationale: A natural complete classification of full automorphisms of complete-bipartite graph evolution algebras is relevant to a recent explicit question about Ramanujan evolution algebra symmetry. The answer shows two previously absent orthogonal factors (continuous in sufficiently high dimension), a sharp arithmetic cubic-root factor, a balanced graph exchange, exact finite-field group orders and a dimension-one nonsmoothness jump in characteristic three. The object and invariants are natural rather than artificially chosen; the theorem does not purport to solve the full open problem.
